NONE: › a large picture that has been painted on the wall of a room or building
壁畫
B1 the crime of intentionally killing a person
謀殺，兇殺
B1 to commit the crime of intentionally killing a person
謀殺，殺害
› informal If you say you will or could murder someone, you mean you are very angry with them.
（表示非常生氣）決不會原諒
› informal to do or perform something very badly, so that you spoil it completely
破壞，糟蹋；把…弄糟

example: Two sisters have been charged with (= officially accused of) murder.
兩姐妹被控謀殺。
There were three murders in the town last year.
去年鎮上發生了三件謀殺案。
The three were convicted of (= proved guilty of) murder.
這三人被判犯有謀殺罪。
a murder weapon (= a weapon used to commit a murder)
兇器
Compare
manslaughter
Her husband was murdered by gunmen as she watched.
她親眼目睹丈夫被持槍歹徒殺害。
In the last year, terrorists have murdered several local journalists.
去年，恐怖分子殺害了幾名當地記者。
If he's late again, I'll murder him!
如果他再遲到，我決不會原諒他！
karaoke singers who murder pop classics
糟蹋經典流行歌曲的卡拉OK歌手

NONE: B1 someone who illegally and intentionally kills another person
殺人犯，兇手

example: A convicted murderer was executed in North Carolina yesterday.
昨天一名已定罪的殺人犯在北卡羅來納州被處決。
a mass murderer (= someone who has killed a large number of people illegally)
殺人狂

NONE: › extremely dangerous and likely to commit murder
殺人的；兇惡的，兇殘的
› informal extremely unpleasant
令人非常難受的

example: He was a murderous gangster.
他是個殺人不眨眼的歹徒。
She gave me a look of murderous hatred.
她惡狠狠地看了我一眼。
The traffic was murderous today.
今天的交通堵得要命。

NONE: › darkness or thick cloud, preventing you from seeing clearly
黑暗，昏暗；濃雲

example: It was foggy and the sun shone feebly through the murk.
霧氣瀰漫，濃霧中透射出微弱的陽光。

NONE: › dark and dirty or difficult to see through
黑暗的；不清楚的；骯髒的
› used to describe a situation that is complicated and unpleasant, and about which many facts are not clear
（形勢）複雜難懂的，不明朗的

example: The river was brown and murky after the storm.
暴風雨過後，河水變成了褐色，渾濁不清。
He became involved in the murky world of international drug-dealing.
他捲入了陰暗複雜的跨國販毒生意中。
I don't want to get into the murky waters of family arguments.
我不想淌家庭糾紛這道渾水。

NONE: › a situation that is not well known and may be dangerous
陌生的領域；可能會有危險的情況

example: In the last two chapters of the book, she enters the murky waters of male sexuality.
在該書的最後兩章，她提到了男性性行為這個可能會引起麻煩的話題。
After the Wall Street crash, the American economy moved into uncharted waters.
在華爾街股市暴跌之後，美國經濟進入了一個前途未蔔的時期。

I or T: C2 [ I or T ] to speak or say something very quietly

I: › [ I ] to complain about something that you disagree with or dislike, but not in a public way

C: C2 [ C ] the sound of something being said very quietly
› [ C ] a complaint that is expressed privately

example: [ + speech ] "I love you," she murmured.
「我愛你，」她低聲說。
He was murmuring to himself.
他正喃喃自語。
humorous He murmured sweet nothings (= romantic talk) in her ear.
他在她耳邊低聲說著情話。
They were murmuring about the boss's nephew getting the job.
他們私下嘀咕著老闆的姪子得到了那份工作的事。
A murmur of agreement came from the crowd.
人群中傳來了低聲的讚許。
The murmur of the waves on the beach lulled me to sleep.
海浪輕輕拍打著海岸的聲音催我入眠。
After the report was published, there were murmurs of discontent around the office.
報告公佈後，辦公室裡到處是嘀咕和抱怨。

NONE: › the principle that if it is possible for something to go wrong, it will go wrong
莫非定律（一種認為凡有可能出差錯的事終將出差錯的論斷）

example: The bus is always late but today when I was late it came on time - that's Murphy's law!
那一路公車總是延誤，可是今天我遲到了，它卻準時來了——我想那一定是莫非定律在起作用。
